Two small notes: ziehen = hat gezogen when you pull something, but ist (um)gezogen when you move house. hängen is irregular (hing, gehangen) when something IS hanging; when you hang something UP it is regular: hat gehängt.
Common mistake: modal verbs + another verb use a double infinitive in Perfekt: Ich habe arbeiten müssen — but at B1 just say Ich musste arbeiten (Präteritum). Simpler and correct.

🗣️ Say it out loud — the 22 verbs that only live in this table

Read each trio out loud twice — sentence 1 = now, sentence 2 = the yesterday-sandwich, sentence 3 = a twist (question, modal, weil…). Your mouth learns the verb, not your eyes.

bieten — to offer

Die Firma bietet gute Arbeitszeiten.The company offers good working hours.Now-form: the verb sits in slot 2, right after "die Firma".
Das Hotel hat uns ein tolles Frühstück geboten.The hotel offered us a great breakfast.hat-club: offering means no travel and no change — hat geboten.
Schön, dass die Schule auch Abendkurse bietet.Nice that the school also offers evening courses.dass kicks the verb all the way to the end of the sentence.

bitten — to ask, request

Ich bitte dich um ein bisschen Geduld.I'm asking you for a little patience.Now-form in slot 2 — and bitten always comes with "um": bitten um etwas.
Er hat mich um Hilfe gebeten.He asked me for help.hat-club: asking someone is no travel, no change — hat gebeten.
Bittest du sie um eine zweite Chance?Are you asking her for a second chance?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1.

brechen — to break

Er bricht die Schokolade in zwei Stücke.He breaks the chocolate into two pieces.brechen changes its vowel with du and er: er bricht, not "er brecht".
Ich habe mir das Bein gebrochen.I broke my leg.hat-club: I broke something — I didn't travel anywhere myself.
Vorsicht, das Glas kann leicht brechen.Careful, the glass can break easily.Modal bracket: kann sits in slot 2, brechen waits at the very end.

dürfen — to be allowed to

Ich darf hier leider nicht parken.Unfortunately I'm not allowed to park here.Modal bracket: darf in slot 2, the other verb goes to the end.
Als Kind habe ich das nicht gedurft.As a child I wasn't allowed to do that.hat-club: hat gedurft — but only when there is no second verb in the sentence.
Er ist traurig, weil er nicht mitspielen darf.He is sad because he's not allowed to join the game.weil kicks the verb to the very end — even behind mitspielen.

fangen — to catch

Der Torwart fängt den Ball sehr sicher.The goalkeeper catches the ball very safely.fangen changes its vowel with du and er: er fängt.
Die Katze hat eine Maus gefangen.The cat caught a mouse.hat-club: catching something is no travel, no change — hat gefangen.
Fang bitte den Ball!Catch the ball, please!Command form: the verb comes first, and the "du" disappears.

halten — to hold, stop

Der Zug hält nicht an jedem Bahnhof.The train doesn't stop at every station.halten changes its vowel with du and er: er hält.
Er hat sein Versprechen gehalten.He kept his promise.hat-club: holding or keeping something is no travel, no change.
Wo hält der Bus zum Flughafen?Where does the bus to the airport stop?W-question: the W-word comes first, the verb comes second.

hängen — to hang (be hanging)

Die Jacke hängt an der Tür.The jacket is hanging on the door.Now-form in slot 2 — the jacket just hangs there by itself.
Das Foto hat lange im Wohnzimmer gehangen.The photo hung in the living room for a long time.hat-club: the photo stays in one place — no travel, no change.
Hängt der Schlüssel wieder am Haken?Is the key hanging on the hook again?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1.

heißen — to be called

Ich heiße Sadman und lerne Deutsch.My name is Sadman and I'm learning German.Now-form in slot 2 — this is THE sentence for introducing yourself.
Die Straße hat früher anders geheißen.The street used to have a different name.hat-club: having a name is no travel, no change — hat geheißen.
Wie heißt du mit Nachnamen?What is your last name?W-question: "Wie" first, verb second — and du heißt keeps just one t.

können — can, to be able to

Ich kann heute leider nicht kommen.Unfortunately I can't come today.Modal bracket: kann in slot 2, the other verb waits at the end.
Früher habe ich das richtig gut gekonnt.I used to be really good at that.hat-club: hat gekonnt — but only when there is no second verb.
Sie sagt, dass sie gut kochen kann.She says that she can cook well.dass kicks the verb to the very end — even behind kochen.

leihen — to lend, borrow

Ich leihe meinem Bruder zwanzig Euro.I'm lending my brother twenty euros.leihen has a Dativ partner — the person: meinem Bruder.
Sie hat mir ihr Wörterbuch geliehen.She lent me her dictionary.hat-club: lending is no travel, no change — hat geliehen. "mir" is the Dativ partner.
Leihst du mir kurz dein Ladekabel?Will you lend me your charging cable for a moment?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1 — mir is again Dativ.

liegen — to lie, be lying

Das Handy liegt auf dem Küchentisch.The phone is lying on the kitchen table.Now-form in slot 2 — the phone just lies there by itself.
Ich habe den ganzen Sonntag im Bett gelegen.I lay in bed all Sunday.hat-club: lying down is staying in one spot — no travel from A to B.
Wo liegt deine neue Wohnung?Where is your new flat?W-question: "Wo" first, verb second.

nennen — to name, call

Wir nennen unseren Hund einfach Bello.We simply call our dog Bello.Now-form in slot 2, right after "wir".
Der Lehrer hat drei Beispiele genannt.The teacher named three examples.hat-club: naming something is no travel, no change — hat genannt.
Nenn mir bitte deinen vollen Namen!Please tell me your full name!Command form: the verb comes first, no "du".

rufen — to call, shout

Das Kind ruft laut nach seiner Mutter.The child is calling loudly for its mother.Now-form: the verb sits in slot 2.
Wir haben sofort einen Arzt gerufen.We called a doctor right away.hat-club: calling out is no travel, no change — hat gerufen.
Du musst lauter rufen, er hört schlecht.You have to shout louder, he hears badly.Modal bracket: musst in slot 2, rufen at the end of its part.

scheinen — to shine, seem

Die Sonne scheint heute den ganzen Tag.The sun is shining all day today.Now-form in slot 2, right after "die Sonne".
Gestern hat die Sonne kaum geschienen.Yesterday the sun hardly shone.hat-club: shining is no travel, no change — hat geschienen.
Scheint bei euch auch die Sonne?Is the sun shining where you are too?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1.

schwimmen — to swim

Du schwimmst wirklich schneller als ich.You really swim faster than I do.Now-form in slot 2 — du always adds -st: du schwimmst.
Er ist gestern eine Stunde geschwommen.He swam for an hour yesterday.ist-club: swimming is travelling from A to B through the water — ist geschwommen.
Ich kann leider nicht sehr gut schwimmen.Unfortunately I can't swim very well.Modal bracket: kann in slot 2, schwimmen waits at the end.

singen — to sing

Meine Schwester singt gern unter der Dusche.My sister likes singing in the shower.Now-form: the verb sits in slot 2.
Wir haben auf der Party laut gesungen.We sang loudly at the party.hat-club: singing is no travel, no change — hat gesungen.
Warum singst du so früh am Morgen?Why are you singing so early in the morning?W-question: "Warum" first, verb second.

sitzen — to sit, be sitting

Oma sitzt am Fenster und liest.Grandma is sitting at the window reading.Now-form in slot 2 — she just sits there.
Ich habe drei Stunden im Zug gesessen.I sat on the train for three hours.hat-club: sitting means staying put — no travel from A to B.
Mein Rücken tut weh, weil ich zu viel sitze.My back hurts because I sit too much.weil kicks the verb to the very end.

stehen — to stand

Das Auto steht vor der Garage.The car is standing in front of the garage.Now-form in slot 2 — the car just stands there.
Wir haben lange an der Kasse gestanden.We stood at the checkout for a long time.hat-club: standing means staying put — no travel, no change.
Steht dein Name schon auf der Liste?Is your name on the list yet?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1.

sterben — to die

Ohne Wasser stirbt die Pflanze schnell.Without water the plant dies quickly.sterben changes its vowel with du and er: sie stirbt.
Sein Großvater ist letztes Jahr gestorben.His grandfather died last year.ist-club: dying is a change of state — alive to not alive — so ist gestorben.
Es ist traurig, dass so viele Bienen sterben.It is sad that so many bees are dying.dass kicks the verb to the very end.

tun — to do

Ich tue alles für meine Familie.I do everything for my family.Now-form in slot 2 — tun is the short cousin of machen.
Er hat den ganzen Tag nichts getan.He did nothing all day.hat-club: doing (or not doing!) is no travel, no change — hat getan.
Was tust du gerade in der Küche?What are you doing in the kitchen right now?W-question: "Was" first, verb second.

waschen — to wash

Er wäscht sein Auto jeden Samstag.He washes his car every Saturday.waschen changes its vowel with du and er: er wäscht.
Ich habe gestern alle Handtücher gewaschen.I washed all the towels yesterday.hat-club: washing is no travel, no change — hat gewaschen.
Wasch dir vor dem Essen die Hände!Wash your hands before eating!Command form: verb first — and "dir" says whose hands they are.

ziehen — to pull

Der Hund zieht stark an der Leine.The dog is pulling hard on the leash.Now-form: the verb sits in slot 2.
Wir haben den Tisch in die Ecke gezogen.We pulled the table into the corner.hat-club: pulling something is no travel for YOU — hat gezogen. (Moving house is different: ist umgezogen.)
Ich kann den schweren Koffer kaum ziehen.I can hardly pull the heavy suitcase.Modal bracket: kann in slot 2, ziehen waits at the end.
🔑 Everyday basics 15 verbs
InfinitivEnglishPerfekt
seinto beist gewesen
habento havehat gehabt
werdento becomeist geworden
machento do, makehat gemacht
gehento goist gegangen
kommento comeist gekommen
gebento givehat gegeben
nehmento takehat genommen
sehento seehat gesehen
findento find, thinkhat gefunden
bleibento stayist geblieben
wissento know (facts)hat gewusst
kennento know (people, places)hat gekannt
brauchento needhat gebraucht
lassento let, leavehat gelassen

🗣️ Say it out loud — 3 sentences for every verb

Read each trio out loud twice — sentence 1 = now, sentence 2 = the yesterday-sandwich, sentence 3 = a twist (question, modal, weil…). Your mouth learns the verb, not your eyes.

sein — to be

Ich bin heute sehr müde.I am very tired today.sein is totally irregular: ich bin, du bist, er ist — learn the trio by heart.
Ich bin letzte Woche krank gewesen.I was ill last week.sein rides in the ist-club (being is a state, not an action) — and in real speech Germans usually say "ich war"; both are correct.
Bist du morgen wieder im Büro?Are you back in the office tomorrow?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1, before du.

haben — to have

Du hast ein sehr schönes Auto.You have a very nice car.haben drops its b with du and er: du hast, er hat.
Ich habe gestern keine Zeit gehabt.I had no time yesterday.No travel, no change → hat-club. In everyday speech "ich hatte" is the favourite — both are correct.
Wann hast du endlich Zeit für mich?When do you finally have time for me?W-question: the question word comes first, the verb sits in place two.

werden — to become

Mein Bruder wird nächstes Jahr dreißig.My brother turns thirty next year.werden changes with du and er: du wirst, er wird.
Meine Schwester ist Ärztin geworden.My sister became a doctor.Becoming = changing state → ist-club.
Ich will später Pilotin werden.I want to become a pilot one day.Modal bracket: "will" takes place two, the main verb waits at the very end.

machen — to do, make

Wir machen am Sonntag einen Ausflug.We are going on a day trip on Sunday.machen is fully regular — wir always gets the full -en ending.
Wir haben gestern die Hausaufgaben gemacht.We did the homework yesterday.No travel, no change → hat-club: hat gemacht.
Ich bin fit, weil ich jeden Tag Sport mache.I am fit because I do sport every day.weil kicks the verb to the very end of its part.

gehen — to go

Ich gehe jeden Morgen zu Fuß zur Arbeit.I walk to work every morning.Regular now-form: ich gehe, du gehst, er geht.
Er ist gestern früh nach Hause gegangen.He went home early yesterday.Going = travelling from A to B → ist-club: ist gegangen.
Geh doch morgen zum Arzt!Go to the doctor tomorrow!Command form: verb first, and the du disappears.

kommen — to come

Er kommt immer zu spät zur Arbeit.He always comes to work too late.Regular now-form: er gets the -t ending: er kommt.
Sie ist gestern spät nach Hause gekommen.She came home late yesterday.Coming = travelling from A to B → ist-club: ist gekommen.
Kommst du am Samstag zu meiner Party?Are you coming to my party on Saturday?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1.

geben — to give

Er gibt mir seine Telefonnummer.He gives me his phone number.geben changes its vowel with du and er: du gibst, er gibt — and the receiver is a Dativ person: MIR.
Der Lehrer hat uns viele Hausaufgaben gegeben.The teacher gave us a lot of homework.No travel, no change → hat-club: hat gegeben.
Was gibst du deinem Vater zum Geburtstag?What are you giving your father for his birthday?W-question: "Was" first, verb second — and the receiver (deinem Vater) is Dativ again.

nehmen — to take

Du nimmst immer das größte Stück Kuchen.You always take the biggest piece of cake.nehmen changes its vowel with du and er: du nimmst, er nimmt.
Ich habe heute Morgen den Zug genommen.I took the train this morning.nehmen is grabbing something, not travelling → hat-club: hat genommen.
Nimm den Bus, das Taxi ist teuer!Take the bus, the taxi is expensive!Command form: verb first — and it keeps the changed vowel: Nimm!

sehen — to see

Sie sieht ihre Oma jedes Wochenende.She sees her grandma every weekend.sehen changes its vowel with du and er: du siehst, er sieht.
Wir haben den Film schon zweimal gesehen.We have already seen the film twice.No travel, no change → hat-club: hat gesehen.
Ich möchte diesen Film unbedingt sehen.I really want to see this film.Modal bracket: "möchte" sits in place two, the main verb parks at the end.

finden — to find, think

Ich finde deine Idee wirklich gut.I think your idea is really good.finden also means "to think something is …" — Germans use it all the time for opinions.
Ich habe meinen Schlüssel endlich gefunden.I finally found my key.No travel, no change → hat-club: hat gefunden.
Ich hoffe, dass du bald eine Wohnung findest.I hope that you find a flat soon.dass kicks the verb to the very end of its part.

bleiben — to stay

Wir bleiben heute lieber zu Hause.We would rather stay home today.Regular now-form: wir bleiben, with the full -en ending.
Ich bin am Wochenende zu Hause geblieben.I stayed home at the weekend.bleiben travels nowhere — but it is a famous exception and still joins the ist-club: ist geblieben.
Bleibst du heute Abend bei uns?Are you staying with us tonight?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1.

wissen — to know (facts)

Ich weiß die Antwort leider nicht.Unfortunately I don't know the answer.wissen is irregular: ich weiß, du weißt — and it is only for facts, like an answer.
Ich habe seinen Namen nicht gewusst.I didn't know his name.No travel, no change → hat-club: hat gewusst.
Woher weißt du das denn?How do you know that?W-question: "Woher" first, verb second — wissen because "that" is a fact.

kennen — to know (people, places)

Ich kenne einen guten Zahnarzt in Berlin.I know a good dentist in Berlin.kennen is for people and places you are familiar with — a dentist is a person, so kennen, not wissen.
Ich habe seine Frau lange gekannt.I knew his wife for a long time.No travel, no change → hat-club: hat gekannt.
Ich frage dich, weil du die Stadt gut kennst.I'm asking you because you know the city well.weil kicks the verb to the end — and a city is a place, so kennen.

brauchen — to need

Ihr braucht warme Jacken für den Winter.You (all) need warm jackets for the winter.Regular now-form: ihr always gets the -t ending: ihr braucht.
Ich habe gestern deine Hilfe gebraucht.I needed your help yesterday.No travel, no change → hat-club: hat gebraucht.
Brauchst du noch etwas aus dem Supermarkt?Do you need anything else from the supermarket?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1.

lassen — to let, leave

Ich lasse mein Handy reparieren.I'm having my phone repaired.lassen + a second verb at the end = you let someone else do it for you.
Ich habe meine Tasche im Bus gelassen.I left my bag on the bus.No travel, no change (the bag just stays there) → hat-club: hat gelassen.
Lass mich bitte in Ruhe arbeiten!Please let me work in peace!Command form: verb first, no du — Lass!

sagento sayhat gesagt

fragento askhat gefragt
antwortento answerhat geantwortet
erzählento tell, narratehat erzählt
erklärento explainhat erklärt
verstehento understandhat verstanden
denkento thinkhat gedacht
glaubento believehat geglaubt
meinento mean, thinkhat gemeint
beschreibento describehat beschrieben
lesento readhat gelesen
schreibento writehat geschrieben
hörento hearhat gehört

empfehlento recommendhat empfohlen

🗣️ Say it out loud — 3 sentences for every verb

Read each trio out loud twice — sentence 1 = now, sentence 2 = the yesterday-sandwich, sentence 3 = a twist (question, modal, weil…). Your mouth learns the verb, not your eyes.

sagen — to say

Ich sage immer die Wahrheit.I always tell the truth.The ich-form ends in -e: ich sage.
Er hat gestern nichts gesagt.He said nothing yesterday.No travel, no change → hat-club; regular sandwich: ge…t = gesagt.
Sie sagt, dass sie morgen kommt.She says that she is coming tomorrow.dass kicks the verb to the very end of its part.

sprechen — to speak

Du sprichst schon sehr gut Deutsch.You already speak German very well.sprechen changes its vowel with du and er: du sprichst.
Wir haben lange mit dem Chef gesprochen.We talked with the boss for a long time.No travel, no change → haben-club; the ge-word gesprochen closes the sandwich.
Sprichst du auch ein bisschen Englisch?Do you also speak a little English?Yes/no question — the verb jumps to position 1.

reden — to talk

Ihr redet heute wirklich zu laut.You are really talking too loudly today.The stem ends in d, so we add -et: ihr redet.
Sie hat viel über die Arbeit geredet.She talked a lot about work.No travel, no change → hat-club; d-stem again: ge…et = geredet.
Wir müssen über das Problem reden.We have to talk about the problem.müssen takes spot 2, so reden waits at the very end.

fragen — to ask

Sie fragt den Lehrer sehr viel.She asks the teacher a lot.The er/sie-form ends in -t: sie fragt.
Ich habe ihn nach dem Weg gefragt.I asked him for directions.No travel, no change → habe-club; regular sandwich: ge…t = gefragt.
Frag doch einfach deine Nachbarin!Just ask your neighbour!Command to du — verb goes first and the du disappears.

antworten — to answer

Du antwortest immer sehr schnell.You always answer very quickly.The stem ends in t, so we add -est: du antwortest.
Sie hat mir sofort geantwortet.She answered me right away.No travel, no change → hat-club; and antworten wants a Dativ partner: sie antwortet MIR.
Warum antwortet er nicht auf meine Mail?Why isn't he answering my email?W-word first, verb second — always.

erzählen — to tell, narrate

Oma erzählt uns eine lustige Geschichte.Grandma tells us a funny story.The er/sie-form ends in -t: sie erzählt.
Er hat uns von seiner Reise erzählt.He told us about his trip.No travel, no change → hat-club; er- verbs never get ge-: erzählt.
Erzähl mir alles über die Party!Tell me everything about the party!Command — the verb jumps to the front.

erklären — to explain

Der Lehrer erklärt die Aufgabe gut.The teacher explains the task well.The er-form ends in -t: er erklärt.
Sie hat mir die Regel erklärt.She explained the rule to me.No travel, no change → hat-club; er- verbs skip ge-: erklärt.
Kannst du mir das kurz erklären?Can you explain that to me quickly?kannst sits up front, erklären waits at the very end.

verstehen — to understand

Ich verstehe diese Frage leider nicht.Unfortunately I don't understand this question.The ich-form ends in -e: ich verstehe.
Wir haben den Film gut verstanden.We understood the film well.No travel, no change → haben-club; ver- verbs never get ge-: verstanden.
Verstehst du mich jetzt besser?Do you understand me better now?Yes/no question — the verb goes first.

denken — to think

Er denkt oft an seine Familie.He often thinks of his family.The er-form ends in -t: er denkt.
Ich habe gestern an dich gedacht.I thought about you yesterday.No travel, no change → habe-club; denken is irregular: gedacht, not gedenkt.
Was denkst du über meinen Plan?What do you think about my plan?W-word first, verb in spot 2.

glauben — to believe

Wir glauben dir kein Wort.We don't believe a word you say.The wir-form looks like the infinitive: wir glauben.
Sie hat seine Geschichte nicht geglaubt.She didn't believe his story.No travel, no change → hat-club; regular sandwich: ge…t = geglaubt.
Ich glaube, dass es morgen regnet.I believe that it will rain tomorrow.dass kicks the verb to the end of its part.

meinen — to mean, think

Ich meine das wirklich ernst.I really mean that seriously.The ich-form ends in -e: ich meine.
So hat er das nicht gemeint.He didn't mean it like that.No travel, no change → hat-club; regular sandwich: ge…t = gemeint.
Was meinst du mit diesem Satz?What do you mean by this sentence?W-word first, verb second.

beschreiben — to describe

Sie beschreibt ihre neue Wohnung.She describes her new flat.The sie-form ends in -t: sie beschreibt.
Er hat den Weg genau beschrieben.He described the way exactly.No travel, no change → hat-club; be- verbs skip ge-: beschrieben.
Beschreib mir bitte dein Traumhaus!Please describe your dream house to me!Command to du — verb first, no du.

lesen — to read

Er liest jeden Morgen die Zeitung.He reads the newspaper every morning.lesen changes its vowel with du and er: er liest.
Ich habe das Buch schon gelesen.I have already read the book.No travel, no change → habe-club; strong sandwich: ge…en = gelesen.
Ich will heute Abend noch lesen.I still want to read this evening.will takes spot 2, so lesen goes to the very end.

schreiben — to write

Du schreibst mir nie eine Nachricht.You never write me a message.The du-form ends in -st: du schreibst.
Sie hat gestern eine E-Mail geschrieben.She wrote an email yesterday.No travel, no change → hat-club; strong sandwich: ge…en = geschrieben.
Ich freue mich, wenn du mir schreibst.I'm happy when you write to me.wenn kicks the verb to the end of its part.

hören — to hear

Ich höre gern Musik beim Kochen.I like listening to music while cooking.The ich-form ends in -e: ich höre.
Wir haben ein lautes Geräusch gehört.We heard a loud noise.No travel, no change → haben-club; regular sandwich: ge…t = gehört.
Hörst du die Vögel draußen?Do you hear the birds outside?Yes/no question — verb jumps to position 1.

wiederholen — to repeat

Der Lehrer wiederholt die Frage langsam.The teacher slowly repeats the question.The er-form ends in -t — and wieder- stays glued on, it never splits off.
Ich habe die Wörter dreimal wiederholt.I repeated the words three times.No travel, no change → habe-club; wiederholen skips ge- completely: wiederholt.
Wiederholen Sie das bitte langsam!Please repeat that slowly!Polite command — verb first, then Sie.

bedeuten — to mean

Das Wort bedeutet etwas Schönes.The word means something beautiful.The stem ends in t, so we add -et: es bedeutet.
Deine Hilfe hat mir viel bedeutet.Your help meant a lot to me.No travel, no change → hat-club; be- verbs get no ge-: bedeutet.
Was bedeutet dieses Wort auf Deutsch?What does this word mean in German?W-word first, verb second.

empfehlen — to recommend

Der Kellner empfiehlt uns den Fisch.The waiter recommends the fish to us.empfehlen changes its vowel with du and er: er empfiehlt.
Sie hat mir dieses Hotel empfohlen.She recommended this hotel to me.No travel, no change → hat-club; emp- verbs skip ge-: empfohlen.
Kannst du mir ein Restaurant empfehlen?Can you recommend a restaurant to me?kannst sits up front, empfehlen waits at the end.

vergessen — to forget

Er vergisst immer seinen Schlüssel.He always forgets his key.vergessen changes its vowel with du and er: er vergisst.
Ich habe deinen Geburtstag vergessen.I forgot your birthday.No travel, no change → habe-club; ver- verbs never get ge-: vergessen.
Vergiss deine Tasche nicht!Don't forget your bag!Command to du — verb first, and the vowel changes too: Vergiss!

entscheiden — to decide

Sie entscheidet das ganz allein.She decides that all by herself.The stem ends in d, so we add -et: sie entscheidet.
Der Chef hat das sehr schnell entschieden.The boss decided that very quickly.No travel, no change → hat-club; ent- verbs skip ge-: entschieden.
Wir warten, weil der Chef heute entscheidet.We are waiting because the boss decides today.weil kicks the verb to the very end.

Gestern bin ich um sechs Uhr aufgestanden und habe Frühstück gemacht.Yesterday I got up at six o'clock and made breakfast.

🗣️ Say it out loud — 3 sentences for every verb

Read each trio out loud twice — sentence 1 = now, sentence 2 = the yesterday-sandwich, sentence 3 = a twist (question, modal, weil…). Your mouth learns the verb, not your eyes.

fahren — to drive, go

Er fährt jeden Tag mit dem Bus.He goes by bus every day.fahren changes its vowel with du and er: er fährt.
Wir sind gestern nach Berlin gefahren.We drove to Berlin yesterday.ist-club: you travel from A to B (home → Berlin).
Fährst du morgen zur Arbeit?Are you driving to work tomorrow?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1.

fliegen — to fly

Ich fliege im August nach Spanien.I'm flying to Spain in August.Now-form with ich: just the normal ending -e.
Sie ist letztes Jahr nach Rom geflogen.She flew to Rome last year.ist-club: flying is travelling from A to B (here → Rome).
Wir wollen bald nach Griechenland fliegen.We want to fly to Greece soon.Modal bracket: wollen sits in spot 2, fliegen waits at the end.

laufen — to run, walk

Du läufst wirklich sehr schnell.You really run very fast.laufen changes its vowel with du and er: du läufst.
Ich bin heute zum Bahnhof gelaufen.I walked to the station today.ist-club: your legs carry you from A to B (home → station).
Ich nehme den Bus, weil ich nicht gern laufe.I take the bus because I don't like walking.weil kicks the verb to the very end of its part.

reisen — to travel

Wir reisen gern durch Europa.We like travelling through Europe.Now-form with wir: same as the dictionary form.
Sie ist allein durch Asien gereist.She travelled through Asia alone.ist-club: travelling is moving from place to place, A to B.
Wohin reist ihr im Sommer?Where are you travelling to in summer?W-question: W-word first, verb right after it in spot 2.

aufstehen — to get up

Ich stehe jeden Morgen um sieben auf.I get up at seven every morning.Separable verbs throw their prefix to the very end.
Er ist heute sehr spät aufgestanden.He got up very late today.ist-club: a change of state — lying in bed → standing up.
Steh auf, wir sind spät dran!Get up, we're running late!Command: verb first, but the prefix still sits at the end.

einschlafen — to fall asleep

Das Baby schläft sofort ein.The baby falls asleep immediately.Two things: the vowel changes (er schläft) and the prefix flies to the end.
Ich bin vor dem Fernseher eingeschlafen.I fell asleep in front of the TV.ist-club: a change of state — awake → asleep.
Schläfst du immer so früh ein?Do you always fall asleep so early?Yes/no question: verb jumps to position 1, prefix stays at the end.

aufwachen — to wake up

Sie wacht jeden Tag um sechs auf.She wakes up at six every day.Separable verbs throw their prefix to the very end.
Wir sind heute sehr früh aufgewacht.We woke up very early today.ist-club: a change of state — asleep → awake.
Ich trinke Kaffee, wenn ich aufwache.I drink coffee when I wake up.wenn kicks the verb to the end — and the prefix glues back on.

umziehen — to move house

Meine Schwester zieht nächsten Monat um.My sister is moving house next month.Separable verbs throw their prefix to the very end.
Wir sind im Mai nach Köln umgezogen.We moved to Cologne in May.ist-club: a change — old flat → new flat.
Warum zieht ihr schon wieder um?Why are you moving again already?W-question: W-word first, verb in spot 2, prefix at the very end.

passieren — to happen

So etwas passiert hier oft.Something like that happens here often.passieren goes with things (es, das), almost never with people.
Gestern ist ein Unfall passiert.An accident happened yesterday.ist-club: something happens = the situation changes.
Ich hoffe, dass nichts Schlimmes passiert.I hope nothing bad happens.dass kicks the verb to the very end.

steigen — to climb, rise

Die Preise steigen jedes Jahr.Prices rise every year.Now-form with a plural (die Preise): same as the dictionary form.
Er ist auf den Berg gestiegen.He climbed the mountain.ist-club: moving from A to B — bottom → top.
Steigen wir zusammen auf den Berg?Shall we climb the mountain together?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1.

fallen — to fall

Das Glas fällt vom Tisch.The glass falls off the table.fallen changes its vowel with du and er: es fällt.
Das Kind ist vom Fahrrad gefallen.The child fell off the bike.ist-club: moving from A to B — top → bottom.
Vorsicht, das Glas kann fallen!Careful, the glass can fall!Modal bracket: kann in spot 2, fallen waits at the end.

essen — to eat

Du isst heute sehr wenig.You're eating very little today.essen changes its vowel with du and er: du isst.
Wir haben Pizza mit Freunden gegessen.We ate pizza with friends.hat-club: eating is no travel and no change of you.
Was isst du zum Frühstück?What do you eat for breakfast?W-question: W-word first, verb right after it.

trinken — to drink

Ich trinke morgens immer Kaffee.I always drink coffee in the morning.Now-form with ich: just the normal ending -e.
Er hat zu viel Cola getrunken.He drank too much cola.hat-club: drinking is no travel and no change of you.
Trink mehr Wasser, es ist heiß!Drink more water, it's hot!Command: the verb goes first, no du needed.

schlafen — to sleep

Er schläft am Wochenende sehr lange.He sleeps very long at the weekend.schlafen changes its vowel with du and er: er schläft.
Ich habe nur fünf Stunden geschlafen.I only slept five hours.hat-club: sleeping is staying as you are — no travel, no change. (Falling asleep = change = einschlafen with ist!)
Sie ist müde, weil sie schlecht schläft.She is tired because she sleeps badly.weil kicks the verb to the very end.

kochen — to cook

Meine Mutter kocht heute Abend Suppe.My mother is cooking soup tonight.Now-form with sie: ending -t, nothing tricky.
Wir haben zusammen Nudeln gekocht.We cooked pasta together.hat-club: you stand at the stove — no travel, no change of you.
Kochst du heute für uns?Are you cooking for us today?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1.

kaufen — to buy

Ich kaufe Brot beim Bäcker.I buy bread at the bakery.Now-form with ich: just the normal ending -e.
Sie hat gestern ein neues Handy gekauft.She bought a new phone yesterday.hat-club: buying is no travel and no change of you.
Wir wollen ein neues Auto kaufen.We want to buy a new car.Modal bracket: wollen in spot 2, kaufen waits at the end.

einkaufen — to shop

Wir kaufen samstags im Supermarkt ein.We shop at the supermarket on Saturdays.Separable verbs throw their prefix to the very end.
Ich habe für das Wochenende eingekauft.I did the shopping for the weekend.hat-club: shopping is no travel and no change of you — the ge- hides inside: ein-ge-kauft.
Wo kaufst du normalerweise ein?Where do you normally shop?W-question: verb in spot 2, prefix still at the very end.

tragen — to carry, wear

Sie trägt heute ein rotes Kleid.She's wearing a red dress today.tragen changes its vowel with du and er: sie trägt.
Er hat die schweren Taschen getragen.He carried the heavy bags.hat-club: no travel, no change — you just hold something.
Trag bitte die Kisten nach oben!Please carry the boxes upstairs!Command: the verb goes first, no du needed.

bringen — to bring

Ich bringe dir gleich einen Tee.I'll bring you a tea in a moment.Now-form with ich — and the person who gets it is Dativ: dir.
Sie hat die Kinder zur Schule gebracht.She took the children to school.hat-club: bringen always has a "what" you carry — verbs with a "what" take hat. Note the odd form: gebracht, not "gebringt".
Er sagt, dass er einen Kuchen bringt.He says that he's bringing a cake.dass kicks the verb to the very end.

holen — to fetch

Er holt schnell Brötchen vom Bäcker.He's quickly fetching rolls from the bakery.Now-form with er: ending -t, nothing tricky.
Ich habe Getränke aus der Küche geholt.I fetched drinks from the kitchen.hat-club: holen has a "what" you fetch — verbs with a "what" take hat.
Hol bitte die Kinder von der Schule!Please pick the children up from school!Command: the verb goes first, no du needed.

öffnen — to open

Der Laden öffnet um neun Uhr.The shop opens at nine o'clock.Now-form: öffnen keeps an extra e — er öffnet, so you can say it.
Sie hat das Fenster geöffnet.She opened the window.hat-club: no travel, no change of you — the window changes, not you.
Kannst du bitte die Tür öffnen?Can you please open the door?Modal bracket: kannst jumps to spot 1 for the question, öffnen waits at the end.

schließen — to close

Ich schließe abends alle Fenster.I close all the windows in the evening.Now-form with ich: just the normal ending -e.
Er hat die Tür leise geschlossen.He closed the door quietly.hat-club: no travel, no change of you — the door changes, not you.
Wann schließt der Supermarkt heute?When does the supermarket close today?W-question: W-word first, verb right after it in spot 2.

🗣️ Say it out loud — 3 sentences for every verb

Read each trio out loud twice — sentence 1 = now, sentence 2 = the yesterday-sandwich, sentence 3 = a twist (question, modal, weil…). Your mouth learns the verb, not your eyes.

mögen — to like

Ich mag Kaffee mit viel Milch.I like coffee with lots of milk.mögen is a rebel: ich mag — no -e ending, and the vowel changes.
Ich habe den Film sehr gemocht.I really liked the film.hat-club: liking is no travel and no change — helper habe, gemocht at the end.
Magst du italienisches Essen?Do you like Italian food?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1, the person comes after.

gefallen — to please (+Dativ)

Der Film gefällt mir sehr gut.I like the film a lot (it pleases me).gefallen changes its vowel: er gefällt — and the person who likes it goes in Dativ: MIR.
Das Konzert hat uns gut gefallen.We liked the concert.hat-club: no travel, no change. gefallen already starts with ge-, so it gets no extra ge-.
Wie gefällt dir deine neue Wohnung?How do you like your new flat?W-question: the question word is first, the verb sits in spot 2 — dir is the Dativ partner.

lieben — to love

Wir lieben unsere Kinder sehr.We love our children very much.Normal now-form: wir gets the full -en ending, verb in spot 2.
Er hat seine Frau immer geliebt.He always loved his wife.hat-club: loving is no travel and no change — helper hat, ge-word geliebt at the end.
Ich weiß, dass du mich liebst.I know that you love me.dass kicks the verb all the way to the end of its part.

vermissen — to miss (somebody)

Ich vermisse meine Freunde in Berlin.I miss my friends in Berlin.Normal now-form: ich gets -e, verb in spot 2.
Ich habe dich sehr vermisst.I missed you a lot.hat-club: no travel, no change. Verbs starting with ver- get no extra ge-.
Vermisst du dein altes Zuhause?Do you miss your old home?Yes/no question: the verb jumps to position 1.

wünschen — to wish

Ich wünsche dir viel Glück!I wish you good luck!You wish something TO someone — that someone is Dativ: dir.
Er hat mir gute Besserung gewünscht.He wished me a speedy recovery.hat-club: wishing is no travel and no change — hat + gewünscht at the end.
Was wünschst du dir zum Geburtstag?What do you wish for for your birthday?W-question: Was first, verb in spot 2 — dir means "for yourself".

hoffen — to hope

Wir hoffen auf gutes Wetter.We are hoping for good weather.Normal now-form — hoffen always teams up with "auf" for the thing you hope for.
Ich habe lange auf eine Antwort gehofft.I hoped for an answer for a long time.hat-club: hoping is no travel and no change — habe + gehofft at the end.
Wir können jetzt nur noch hoffen.All we can do now is hope.Modal bracket: können sits in spot 2, hoffen waits at the very end.

helfen — to help (+Dativ)

Er hilft seiner Mutter in der Küche.He helps his mother in the kitchen.helfen changes its vowel with du and er: er hilft — and it always forces Dativ: seiner Mutter.
Du hast mir gestern sehr geholfen.You helped me a lot yesterday.hat-club: no travel, no change — hast + geholfen. The helped person is Dativ: MIR.
Hilf mir bitte in der Küche!Please help me in the kitchen!Command: the verb goes first and drops "du" — Hilf! keeps the vowel change.

danken — to thank (+Dativ)

Ich danke dir für deine Hilfe.I thank you for your help.danken always forces Dativ: ich danke DIR, never dich.
Wir haben dem Lehrer gedankt.We thanked the teacher.hat-club: thanking is no travel and no change — dem Lehrer is the Dativ partner.
Ich möchte Ihnen herzlich danken.I would like to thank you warmly.Modal bracket: möchte in spot 2, danken at the very end — Ihnen is polite Dativ.

sich freuen — to be happy

Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende.I am looking forward to the weekend.Mirror-word: ich needs mich. "freuen auf" = happy about something coming.
Du hast dich über das Geschenk gefreut.You were happy about the present.hat-club: no travel, no change — and the mirror-word switches with you: du → dich.
Worüber freut er sich denn so?What is he so happy about?W-question: verb in spot 2 — and er gets the mirror-word sich.

sich ärgern — to be annoyed

Du ärgerst dich oft über den Verkehr.You often get annoyed about the traffic.Mirror-word: du needs dich — "ärgern über" names what annoys you.
Er hat sich über den Fehler geärgert.He was annoyed about the mistake.hat-club: no travel, no change — er keeps his mirror-word sich right after the helper.
Ärgerst du dich über das Wetter?Are you annoyed about the weather?Yes/no question: verb jumps to position 1, the mirror-word dich follows du.

sich fühlen — to feel

Ich fühle mich heute richtig gut.I feel really good today.Mirror-word: ich needs mich — in German you feel "yourself" good.
Sie hat sich gestern krank gefühlt.She felt sick yesterday.hat-club: no travel, no change — sie keeps her mirror-word sich.
Wie fühlst du dich heute?How do you feel today?W-question: Wie first, verb in spot 2 — mirror-word dich matches du.

sich interessieren — to be interested

Er interessiert sich für Fußball.He is interested in football.Mirror-word: er needs sich — "interessieren für" names the topic.
Wir haben uns für Musik interessiert.We were interested in music.hat-club: no travel, no change. Verbs ending in -ieren get no ge- — and wir needs the mirror-word uns.
Sie liest viel, weil sie sich für Bücher interessiert.She reads a lot because she is interested in books.weil kicks the verb to the very end of its part.

lachen — to laugh

Die Kinder lachen laut im Garten.The children are laughing loudly in the garden.Normal now-form: plural gets -en, verb in spot 2.
Wir haben über den Witz gelacht.We laughed about the joke.hat-club: laughing is no travel and no change — haben + gelacht at the end.
Lach doch mal wieder!Come on, laugh again!Command: verb first, "du" disappears — Lach!

weinen — to cry

Das Baby weint die ganze Nacht.The baby cries all night.Normal now-form: es/das gets -t, verb in spot 2.
Sie hat im Kino geweint.She cried at the cinema.hat-club: crying is no travel and no change — hat + geweint at the end.
Du musst doch nicht weinen.You really don't have to cry.Modal bracket: musst in spot 2, weinen waits at the very end.

gewinnen — to win

Unsere Mannschaft gewinnt heute bestimmt.Our team will surely win today.Normal now-form: sie (the team) gets -t, verb in spot 2.
Er hat das Spiel gewonnen.He won the game.hat-club: no travel, no change. gewinnen already starts with ge-, so no extra ge- — just gewonnen.
Wer gewinnt heute das Spiel?Who wins the game today?W-question: Wer first, verb in spot 2.

verlieren — to lose

Ich verliere ständig meine Schlüssel.I constantly lose my keys.Normal now-form: ich gets -e, verb in spot 2.
Wir haben das Spiel leider verloren.Sadly, we lost the game.hat-club: no travel, no change. Verbs starting with ver- get no extra ge- — just verloren.
Hast du dein Handy verloren?Did you lose your phone?Yes/no question in the past: the helper jumps to position 1, the ge-word stays at the end.

🗣️ Say it out loud — 3 sentences for every verb

Read each trio out loud twice — sentence 1 = now, sentence 2 = the yesterday-sandwich, sentence 3 = a twist (question, modal, weil…). Your mouth learns the verb, not your eyes.

arbeiten — to work

Wir versuchen es noch einmal.We're trying it one more time.With wir the verb looks like the dictionary form: wir versuchen.

Du schaffst das ganz sicher.You will definitely manage that.With du the verb ends in -st: du schaffst.

Er trifft seine Kollegen im Café.He meets his colleagues at the café.treffen changes its vowel with du and er: er trifft.

Memory trick — verbs in "chunks"Don't memorise fahren alone. Memorise "Ich bin nach Berlin gefahren." The whole sentence stores the meaning, the Perfekt, and the ist auxiliary in one go. 5 chunk-sentences a day beat 20 lonely infinitives.
🧲 Verbs with fixed prepositions 61 combos — Sprachbausteine gold

First, what is a preposition? One of the tiny direction words: auf, an, mit, von, für, über, um… German has "married" certain verbs to certain tiny words forever: warten + auf (to wait FOR), träumen + von (to dream OF). There is no logic to which word — English does the same thing ("depend ON", "afraid OF") — so never learn "warten" alone, learn "warten auf" as ONE word. These combos are tested directly in Sprachbausteine (the gap-fill part). The case chip shows which form the next word takes: A = Akkusativ (the case for the thing the action happens to) · D = Dativ (the "to/for whom" case).

Ich warte auf den Bus. · Sie träumt von einem Urlaub.I'm waiting for the bus. · She dreams of a holiday.

Words 1

Vocabulary 1 — people, family & feelings

HIGHEST ROI

The words you need to talk about yourself — the number one topic in every part of the exam.

How to learn vocabulary with this guide

1. The gender colour code

Every noun has a colour chip: der = blue, die = red, das = green. Build a picture in your head: imagine der-words frozen ice blue, die-words burning fire red, das-words grass green. Example: der Vater is a father frozen in blue ice. Silly pictures stick!

⚠️ One important exception: in the plural, every German noun uses "die" — even masculine and neuter ones: der Tisch → die Tische, das Buch → die Bücher. This plural "die" is not the feminine article and has no colour meaning. Words that exist only in the plural ("nur Plural") therefore get a grey chip: die Eltern, die Geschwister. Grey = there is no gender to memorise here — just learn the word with "die". Meine Eltern wohnen in Berlin. — My parents live in Berlin.

2. Always learn the plural together

Never learn "Kind". Learn das Kind, -er → die Kinder. The plural ending stands after the comma in every table. "Mütter" means the vowel changes: die Mutter → die Mütter.

3. The 3-step daily method (15 minutes)

  • Read one theme out loud, German + English.
  • Cover the English column with your hand and test yourself. Mark the words you forgot.
  • Use 5 of the words in your own spoken sentences. Say them out loud — speaking is part of the exam!

Why do words change? The X-ray 🩻

You will see der, den and dem for the same word and wonder: why does it keep changing? Here is the whole secret, once and forever: the word itself never changes — it just wears a different jacket depending on its job in the sentence. And there are only three jobs:

  • N The DOER (Nominativ) — the one doing the action. Ask: who is doing it?
  • A The TARGET (Akkusativ) — the thing the action happens to. Ask: what is being seen / bought / eaten?
  • D The RECEIVER — or after little words (Dativ) — the person who gets something, or anything standing after the little words mit, bei, zu, von, aus, nach, seit. These little words always force this jacket, no thinking needed.

Now watch one word — der Hund (the dog) — go through all three jobs. Same dog, three jackets:

Der Hund schläft.The dog sleeps.The dog is the DOER — he is the one sleeping. N The DOER keeps the normal dictionary jacket: der. Nothing changes.
Ich sehe den Hund.I see the dog.Now I am the doer, and the dog is the TARGET — the seeing lands on him. A The TARGET jacket for der-words: der → den. That is the only letter that moves.
Ich spiele mit dem Hund.I play with the dog.The little word mit always forces the Dativ jacket — automatically, every time. D So der becomes dem. Nothing else changes.
The die-words and das-words are lazy: they only change in Dativ (die → der, das → dem). Only der-words change in Akkusativ (der → den). That is 80% of the case system already.
WAITERKeep this one picture in your head: a waiter. The DOER hands a plate to the RECEIVER — and the plate itself is the TARGET.
Der Kellner bringt dem Gast die Suppe.The waiter brings the guest the soup.Der Kellner N = the DOER — he does the bringing, so normal jacket. Dem Gast D = the RECEIVER — he gets something, so der → dem. Die Suppe A = the TARGET — the thing being carried; die is a lazy die-word, so it stays die.

Quick reminder: Nominativ = the DOER (subject), Akkusativ = the TARGET of the action, Dativ = the RECEIVER or after little words like mit/bei/zu/von/aus.

Der Bruder wohnt in Berlin.The brother lives in Berlin.The brother is the doer/subject of the sentence, so he keeps his dictionary jacket: der.
Ich besuche den Bruder.I visit the brother.The brother is the TARGET — the visiting lands on him. For der-words Akkusativ turns der into den.
Ich fahre mit dem Bruder nach Berlin.I travel to Berlin with the brother.The little word "mit" always forces Dativ: der becomes dem. No thinking needed.
Die Schwester ist älter als ich.The sister is older than me.The sister is the subject, so die keeps its normal jacket — nothing changes.
Ich frage die Schwester.I ask the sister.The sister is the TARGET of the asking — but die stays die! Only der-words change in Akkusativ.
Das Geschenk ist von der Schwester.The present is from the sister.The little word "von" forces Dativ, and for die-words Dativ turns die into der. A die-word wearing "der" — that is normal!
Das Kind schläft.The child is sleeping.The child is the doer/subject — das keeps its dictionary jacket.
Ich höre das Kind.I hear the child.The child is the TARGET of the hearing — and das stays das, no change at all in Akkusativ.
Die Oma spielt mit dem Kind.Grandma plays with the child."mit" forces Dativ: das becomes dem — the same jacket der-words wear in Dativ.

Quick reminder: Nominativ = the DOER (subject), Akkusativ = the TARGET of the action, Dativ = the RECEIVER or after little words like mit/bei/zu/von/aus.

Der Bart ist schon grau.The beard is already grey.The beard is the subject of the sentence, so it keeps its dictionary jacket: der.
Ich finde den Bart schön.I think the beard is nice.The beard is the TARGET of "finden": Akkusativ, so der → den.
Mit dem Bart siehst du älter aus.With the beard you look older."mit" forces Dativ: der → dem. Bonus: aussehen is separable — "aus" jumps to the end of the sentence.
Die Brille ist neu.The glasses are new.The glasses (singular in German!) are the subject — die keeps its normal jacket.
Ich suche die Brille.I am looking for the glasses.The glasses are the TARGET of the searching — die stays die in Akkusativ. Only der-words change there.
Mit der Brille sehe ich besser.With the glasses I see better."mit" forces Dativ, and for die-words Dativ turns die into der.
Das Gesicht ist rund.The face is round.The face is the subject — das keeps its jacket, nothing changes.
Ich erkenne das Gesicht.I recognise the face.The face is the TARGET of the recognising — das stays das in Akkusativ. Easy!
Er hat Schokolade im Gesicht.He has chocolate on his face."in" for a place forces Dativ: das becomes dem, and in + dem shrinks to im.

Many feeling verbs need a fixed preposition (warten auf style). Learn them as one block: Angst haben vor, stolz auf, sich freuen auf/über, sich ärgern über, träumen von, sich verlieben in.

Quick reminder: Nominativ = the DOER (subject), Akkusativ = the TARGET of the action, Dativ = the RECEIVER or after little words like mit/bei/zu/von/aus.

Der Freund kommt heute zu Besuch.The friend is coming to visit today.The friend is the doer/subject of the sentence, so he keeps his dictionary jacket: der.
Ich rufe den Freund an.I call the friend.The friend is the TARGET of the call: der → den. Bonus: anrufen is separable — "an" goes to the end.
Ich spreche oft mit dem Freund.I often talk with the friend."mit" forces Dativ: der becomes dem — automatically, every time.
Die Familie wohnt in Dhaka.The family lives in Dhaka.The family is the subject — die keeps its normal jacket.
Ich vermisse die Familie.I miss the family.The family is the TARGET of the missing — die stays die in Akkusativ. Only der-words change there.
Am Wochenende telefoniere ich mit der Familie.At the weekend I talk to the family on the phone."mit" forces Dativ, and for die-words Dativ turns die into der.
Das Gefühl ist ganz normal.The feeling is completely normal.The feeling is the subject — das keeps its dictionary jacket.
Ich kenne das Gefühl.I know the feeling.The feeling is the TARGET of the knowing — das stays das in Akkusativ, no change at all.
Ich vertraue dem Gefühl.I trust the feeling.vertrauen (to trust) treats the feeling like a RECEIVER — you give your trust to it — so it takes Dativ: das → dem.
Memory trickdie Angst sounds like English "angst / anxious" — an anxious person screams "AAAH!". And remember the fixed pair: Angst haben vor — you stand frozen before (vor) the thing you fear.
Memory trickLearn word families, not single words: der Freund (friend) → die Freundin (female friend) → freundlich (friendly) → die Freundschaft (friendship). One root, four words. Same with Glück: das Glück → glücklich. You double your vocabulary for free!
TALK ABOUT YOUR FAMILY — READY SENTENCES
  • Ich habe zwei Geschwister: einen Bruder und eine Schwester. — I have two siblings: a brother and a sister.
  • Meine Eltern wohnen noch in meiner Heimat. — My parents still live in my home country.
  • Ich bin 2020 nach Deutschland gekommen. — I came to Germany in 2020.
  • Ich bin verheiratet und habe eine kleine Tochter. — I am married and have a little daughter.
  • Mein Bruder ist zwei Jahre jünger als ich und sehr lustig. — My brother is two years younger than me and very funny.
  • Am Wochenende telefoniere ich oft mit meiner Familie. — At the weekend I often talk to my family on the phone.
These three themes cover the exam's favourite question: "Erzählen Sie etwas über sich und Ihre Familie." (Tell us about yourself and your family.) Learn them first — you will use them in Speaking Part 1, in the letter, and in the listening test.
Words 2

Vocabulary 2 — home, food & shopping

HIGHEST ROI

The three everyday topics that appear again and again in the B1 exam: your home, food and shopping.

How to read the tables: ⭐ = must-know word — learn these first. After each noun you see the plural: die Wohnung, -en means the plural is die Wohnungen. If the plural changes the vowel, we write it in full: der Apfel, Äpfel. Verbs show their Perfekt (past) form: hat gekauft or ist umgezogen — ist-verbs usually mean movement or change.
🏠 Wohnen — Living & home 70 words

Räume & Haus — Rooms & parts of the house

GermanEnglishExample

🏋️ Fall-Training — watch the article change

Quick reminder: Nominativ = the doer/subject of the sentence, Akkusativ = the thing the action happens to, Dativ = after little words like mit/bei/zu/von/aus/in (place) or the receiver.

Der Kühlschrank ist neu.The fridge is new.The fridge is the doer/subject of the sentence, so it keeps its dictionary article: der.
Ich kaufe den Kühlschrank.I buy the fridge.The fridge is the thing being bought. Only der changes to den here — die and das words look exactly the same in Akkusativ!
Das Gemüse ist im Kühlschrank.The vegetables are in the fridge."in" for a place (where is it?) forces Dativ: der becomes dem, and in + dem shrinks to im.
Die Küche ist groß und hell.The kitchen is big and bright.The kitchen is the subject — the sentence is about it — so it keeps its normal article: die.
Wir putzen die Küche.We clean the kitchen.The kitchen is the thing being cleaned (Akkusativ), but die stays die — relax! Only der-words change here.
Ich koche in der Küche.I cook in the kitchen."in" for a place forces Dativ, and for die-words Dativ turns die into der. Yes, a die-word wearing "der" — that is normal!
Das Fenster ist offen.The window is open.The window is the subject, so nothing happens to its article: das stays das.
Ich mache das Fenster zu.I close the window.The window is the thing being closed (Akkusativ) — and das stays das, no change at all. Easy!
Die Katze sitzt am Fenster.The cat sits at the window."an" for a place (where does it sit?) forces Dativ: das becomes dem, and an + dem shrinks to am.

Common mistake: das Gemüse and das Obst are singular words in German, even though English says "vegetables" and "fruits". So: „Das Gemüse ist frisch." (The vegetables are fresh.) Also: schmecken works with Dativ (the case for the person something happens TO): „Die Pizza schmeckt mir." — I like the pizza (literally: the pizza tastes good to me).

🏋️ Fall-Training — watch the article change

Remember: Nominativ = the doer/subject, Akkusativ = the thing the action happens to, Dativ = after little words like mit/bei/zu/von/aus/nach or the receiver.

Der Kuchen schmeckt super.The cake tastes great.The cake is the subject — it is the one doing the tasting-great — so it keeps its dictionary article: der.
Oma backt den Kuchen.Grandma bakes the cake.Grandma is the doer; the cake is the thing being baked. So der changes to den — der-words are the only ones that change in Akkusativ.
Möchtest du ein Stück von dem Kuchen?Would you like a piece of the cake?"von" always forces Dativ, so der becomes dem. Nothing else changes.
Die Rechnung ist nicht hoch.The bill is not high.The bill is the subject of the sentence, so it keeps its normal article: die.
Ich bezahle die Rechnung.I pay the bill.The bill is the thing being paid (Akkusativ), but die stays die — relax! Nothing to learn here.
Es gibt ein Problem mit der Rechnung.There is a problem with the bill."mit" always forces Dativ, and for die-words Dativ turns die into der. That is the whole trick.
Das Brot ist noch warm.The bread is still warm.The bread is the subject, so its article does not move: das stays das.
Ich schneide das Brot.I cut the bread.The bread is the thing being cut (Akkusativ) — and das stays das, exactly like in the dictionary. Easy win!
Zum Brot esse ich Butter und Käse.With the bread I eat butter and cheese."zu" always forces Dativ: das becomes dem, and zu + dem shrinks to zum.

Careful: rosa, lila and orange never change their ending: „eine rosa Mütze", „ein lila Schal" — no -e, no -en. All other colours take normal adjective endings: „ein rotes Kleid", „die gelbe Jacke". After „in" you write the colour with a capital letter: „Haben Sie das Hemd in Blau?" (Do you have the shirt in blue?)
Memory trickBuild any shade with hell- (light) and dunkel- (dark) glued to the front: hell + blau = hellblau (light blue), dunkel + rot = dunkelrot (dark red). Two prefixes, one rule — and you can describe every colour on the Sprechen picture card.
Careful: die Hose is singular in German! One pair of trousers = eine Hose. So: „Die Hose ist neu." (The trousers are new.) The same works for die Brille (glasses) and die Schere (scissors).

🏋️ Fall-Training — watch the article change

One more time: Nominativ = the doer/subject, Akkusativ = the thing the action happens to, Dativ = after little words like mit/bei/zu/von/aus/nach or the receiver.

Der Supermarkt ist heute geöffnet.The supermarket is open today.The supermarket is the subject — the sentence is about it — so it keeps its dictionary article: der.
Ich finde den Supermarkt nicht.I cannot find the supermarket.I am the doer; the supermarket is the thing being searched for. So der changes to den — that is the only article change in Akkusativ.
Die Milch ist aus dem Supermarkt.The milk is from the supermarket."aus" always forces Dativ, so der becomes dem. Nothing else changes.
Die Jacke ist reduziert.The jacket is reduced.The jacket is the subject of the sentence, so it keeps its normal article: die.
Ich nehme die Jacke.I will take the jacket.The jacket is the thing being taken (Akkusativ), but die stays die — relax, no change for die-words here!
Ich gehe mit der Jacke zur Kasse.I go to the checkout with the jacket."mit" always forces Dativ, and for die-words Dativ turns die into der. A die-word wearing "der" — totally normal.
Das Hemd ist zu teuer.The shirt is too expensive.The shirt is the subject, so its article does not move: das stays das.
Ich probiere das Hemd an.I try on the shirt.The shirt is the thing being tried on (Akkusativ) — and das stays das, exactly like in the dictionary. Nothing to memorise!
Zum Hemd passt eine blaue Hose.Blue trousers go well with the shirt."zu" always forces Dativ: das becomes dem, and zu + dem shrinks to zum.
Memory trickGerman words are LEGO: long words are just small words clicked together. Kühl + Schrank = cold + cupboard = fridge. Wasch + Maschine = wash + machine. Hand + Schuh = hand + shoe = glove! Learn the small parts and you can guess hundreds of words. Bonus rule: the last part decides the gender — der Schrank, so it is also der Kühlschrank; die Karte, so it is die Speisekarte.
Memory trickFood gender hints: most fruits are die (die Banane, die Birne, die Erdbeere, die Zitrone, die Orange, die Traube) — the big exception is der Apfel. Most alcoholic drinks are der (der Wein, der Schnaps) — the big exception is das Bier. And words ending in -e are usually die (die Suppe, die Torte, die Gurke, die Tomate).
BEIM EINKAUFEN — READY SENTENCES
  • Ich hätte gern ein Kilo Äpfel. — I would like a kilo of apples.
  • Was kostet das? — How much is that?
  • Haben Sie dieses Hemd in Größe M? — Do you have this shirt in size M?
  • Kann ich das anprobieren? — Can I try this on?
  • Kann ich das umtauschen? — Can I exchange this?
  • Das ist mir zu teuer. — That is too expensive for me.
  • Kann ich mit Karte zahlen? — Can I pay by card?
  • Sonst noch etwas? — Nein, danke, das ist alles. — Anything else? — No thanks, that is all.
You now have the three most useful word fields for the whole exam. These topics appear in the Hören (listening) announcements, the Lesen (reading) adverts, the letter task and the speaking part 2. Ten minutes of review every day beats two hours once a week.
WORDS 3

Vocabulary 3 — health, daily life & environment

TOP EXAM TOPICS

Health, daily routine, weather and the environment appear in almost every telc B1 exam — in reading, listening AND speaking.

How to read the tables: der = masculine, die = feminine, das = neuter. After the noun you see the plural ending (e.g. -en) or the full plural word (e.g. Köpfe). (nur Sg.) means the word has no plural. For verbs you get the Perfekt form: hat = with "haben", ist = with "sein".

🏋️ Fall-Training — watch the article change

Remember: Nominativ = the doer/subject of the sentence, Akkusativ = the thing the action happens to, Dativ = after little words like mit, bei, zu, von, aus, nach — or the person/thing that receives something.

Der Kopf tut mir weh.My head hurts.The head is the doer/subject of the sentence — it is the thing doing the hurting. So it keeps its dictionary article: der.
Der Arzt untersucht den Kopf.The doctor examines the head.The head is the thing being examined — the action lands on it. That is Akkusativ, and only der-words change here: der becomes den.
Er nickt mit dem Kopf.He nods with his head.mit always forces Dativ, no exceptions. So der becomes dem: mit dem Kopf. Nothing else changes.
Die Hand ist ganz kalt.The hand is completely cold.The hand is the subject — the sentence just says what the hand is like. Subject = Nominativ, so die stays die.
Ich hebe die Hand.I raise my hand.The hand is the thing being raised — Akkusativ. But die stays die — relax! Only der-words change in Akkusativ.
Die Tasse fällt mir aus der Hand.The cup falls out of my hand.aus (out of) always forces Dativ. For die-words, Dativ turns die into der: aus der Hand.
Das Bein tut seit gestern weh.The leg has been hurting since yesterday.The leg is the doer/subject here, so it keeps its dictionary article: das.
Die Ärztin untersucht das Bein.The doctor examines the leg.The leg is the thing being examined — Akkusativ. And das stays das — das-words never change in Akkusativ!
Ich habe Schmerzen im Bein.I have pain in my leg.Here in tells you WHERE the pain sits (nothing is moving), and that means Dativ: das becomes dem. Then in + dem melts into one word: im.

Remember: Nominativ = the doer/subject of the sentence, Akkusativ = the thing the action happens to, Dativ = after little words like mit, bei, zu, von, aus, nach — or the person/thing that receives something.

Der Husten ist seit gestern besser.The cough has been better since yesterday.The cough is the subject — the sentence is about what the cough is doing. Subject = Nominativ, so it keeps der.
Ich habe den Husten schon eine Woche.I have had the cough for a week already.The cough is the thing you "have" — haben points straight at it. That is Akkusativ: der becomes den.
Mit dem Husten bleibst du besser zu Hause.With that cough you had better stay at home.mit always forces Dativ, so der becomes dem: mit dem Husten.
Die Grippe dauert meistens eine Woche.The flu usually lasts a week.The flu is the doer/subject — it is the thing doing the "lasting". So die stays die.
Ich habe die Grippe.I have the flu.The flu is the thing you have — Akkusativ. But die stays die — relax! die-words look exactly the same in Akkusativ.
Er erholt sich langsam von der Grippe.He is slowly recovering from the flu.von always forces Dativ. For die-words that means die becomes der: von der Grippe.
Das Fieber ist endlich weg.The fever is finally gone.The fever is the subject — the sentence says what the fever does. Subject = Nominativ, so das stays das.
Die Mutter misst das Fieber.The mother takes the temperature (measures the fever).The fever is the thing being measured — Akkusativ. And das stays das — das-words never change in Akkusativ!
Nach dem Fieber war er noch schwach.After the fever he was still weak.nach (after) always forces Dativ, so das becomes dem: nach dem Fieber.

Remember: Nominativ = the doer/subject of the sentence, Akkusativ = the thing the action happens to, Dativ = after little words like mit, bei, zu, von, aus, nach — or the person/thing that receives something.

Der Termin ist am Montag um neun.The appointment is on Monday at nine.The appointment is the subject — the sentence just says when it is. Subject = Nominativ, so it keeps der.
Ich muss den Termin leider absagen.Unfortunately I have to cancel the appointment.The appointment is the thing being cancelled — the action lands on it. Akkusativ: der becomes den.
Ich komme pünktlich zum Termin.I arrive at the appointment on time.zu always forces Dativ: der becomes dem. Then zu + dem melts into one word: zum.
Die Apotheke ist heute geschlossen.The pharmacy is closed today.The pharmacy is the subject — the sentence says what it is like. Subject = Nominativ, so die stays die.
Ich finde die Apotheke nicht.I can't find the pharmacy.The pharmacy is the thing being looked for — Akkusativ. But die stays die — relax! die-words never change in Akkusativ.

Hier ist das Rezept.Here is the prescription.The prescription is the subject — the thing that "is here". Subject = Nominativ, so das stays das.
Die Ärztin schreibt das Rezept.The doctor writes the prescription.The prescription is the thing being written — Akkusativ. And das stays das — das-words never change in Akkusativ!
Mit dem Rezept gehe ich zur Apotheke.With the prescription I go to the pharmacy.mit always forces Dativ, so das becomes dem: mit dem Rezept.

Memory trickPair each object with its verb as a mini-story in the bathroom: die Seife → sich waschen, das Shampoo → sich die Haare waschen, die Zahnbürste + die Zahnpasta → sich die Zähne putzen, das Handtuch → sich abtrocknen (to dry oneself). Learning verb + object together makes both stick.

Reflexive verbs like sich duschen, sich anziehen, sich beeilen need a reflexive pronoun (a small word pointing back to yourself): ich ... mich, du ... dich, er/sie ... sich. With a body part it changes to Dativ: Ich putze mir die Zähne. (I brush my teeth.)

Der Techniker repariert die Waschmaschine.The technician repairs the washing machine.The machine is the thing being repaired — Akkusativ. But die stays die — relax! Only der-words change here.
Die Wäsche ist noch in der Waschmaschine.The laundry is still in the washing machine.in tells you WHERE the laundry sits (nothing is moving), and that means Dativ: die becomes der.
Das Haus hat einen kleinen Garten.The house has a small garden.The house is the doer/subject — it is the thing that "has" something. So das stays das.
Ich verlasse das Haus um halb acht.I leave the house at half past seven.The house is the thing being left — Akkusativ. And das stays das — das-words never change in Akkusativ!
Sie geht früh aus dem Haus.She leaves the house early.aus (out of) always forces Dativ, so das becomes dem: aus dem Haus.

🏋️ Fall-Training — watch the article change

Remember: Nominativ = the doer/subject of the sentence, Akkusativ = the thing the action happens to, Dativ = after little words like mit, bei, zu, von, aus, nach — or the person/thing that receives something.

Der Wald ist im Herbst besonders schön.The forest is especially beautiful in autumn.The forest is the subject — the sentence says what it is like. Subject = Nominativ, so it keeps der.
Ich mag den Wald im Winter.I like the forest in winter.The forest is the thing being liked — the action lands on it. Akkusativ: der becomes den.
Wir machen ein Picknick im Wald.We have a picnic in the forest.in tells you WHERE the picnic happens (nothing is moving into the forest), so it takes Dativ: der becomes dem, and in + dem melts into im.
Die Sonne scheint den ganzen Tag.The sun shines all day.The sun is the doer/subject — it is doing the shining. Subject = Nominativ, so die stays die.
Wir genießen die Sonne.We enjoy the sun.The sun is the thing being enjoyed — Akkusativ. But die stays die — relax! die-words never change in Akkusativ.
Die Katze liegt in der Sonne.The cat is lying in the sun.in says WHERE the cat lies (no movement), so it takes Dativ: die becomes der — in der Sonne.
Das Meer ist heute ganz ruhig.The sea is completely calm today.The sea is the subject — the sentence says what it is like. Subject = Nominativ, so das stays das.
Vom Balkon sehe ich das Meer.From the balcony I see the sea.The sea is the thing being seen — Akkusativ. And das stays das — das-words never change in Akkusativ!
Wir machen Urlaub am Meer.We spend our holiday at the sea.an says WHERE the holiday happens (no movement), so it takes Dativ: das becomes dem, and an + dem melts into am.
♻️ Umwelt — Environment 35 words
The environment is a favourite topic in the telc B1 speaking part 2 (talk about a topic) and in reading texts. Learn these words and you have ready material for the oral exam.

🏋️ Fall-Training — watch the article change

Remember: Nominativ = the doer/subject of the sentence, Akkusativ = the thing the action happens to, Dativ = after little words like mit, bei, zu, von, aus, nach — or the person/thing that receives something.

Der Müll stinkt schon.The trash already stinks.The trash is the doer/subject — it is doing the stinking. Subject = Nominativ, so it keeps der.
Ich bringe den Müll raus.I take out the trash.The trash is the thing being carried out — the action lands on it. Akkusativ: der becomes den.
Was machst du mit dem Müll?What do you do with the trash?mit always forces Dativ, so der becomes dem: mit dem Müll.
Die Dose ist leer.The can is empty.The can is the subject — the sentence just says what it is like. Subject = Nominativ, so die stays die.
Ich bringe die Dose zum Supermarkt zurück.I take the can back to the supermarket.The can is the thing being brought back — Akkusativ. But die stays die — relax! die-words never change in Akkusativ.
Auf der Dose ist Pfand.There is a deposit on the can.auf says WHERE the deposit sits (nothing is moving), so it takes Dativ: die becomes der — auf der Dose.
Das Pfand ist 25 Cent pro Flasche.The deposit is 25 cents per bottle.The deposit is the subject — the sentence says how much it is. Subject = Nominativ, so das stays das.
Ich bekomme das Pfand zurück.I get the deposit back.The deposit is the thing you get back — Akkusativ. And das stays das — das-words never change in Akkusativ!
Vom Pfand kaufe ich mir ein Eis.With the deposit money I buy myself an ice cream.von always forces Dativ, so das becomes dem — and von + dem melts into vom.
Memory trickBody parts: every morning in the shower, point at each body part and say it out loud with the article — "der Kopf, der Arm, das Knie, der Fuß ...". After one week you know all 20 without a list. Your body is a flashcard you always carry with you.
Memory trickThe Schmerzen pattern: take any body part and add -schmerzen — Kopfschmerzen, Bauchschmerzen, Halsschmerzen, Rückenschmerzen, Zahnschmerzen. One pattern, five words. Always plural, always with haben: "Ich habe Kopfschmerzen."
BEIM ARZT — READY SENTENCES
  • Ich möchte einen Termin vereinbaren. — I would like to make an appointment.
  • Ich habe seit drei Tagen starke Kopfschmerzen. — I have had a bad headache for three days.
  • Ich bin gegen Nüsse allergisch. — I am allergic to nuts.
  • Brauche ich ein Rezept? — Do I need a prescription?
  • Wie oft muss ich die Tabletten nehmen? — How often do I have to take the tablets?
  • Können Sie mich bitte krankschreiben? — Can you please give me a sick note?
These three themes give you easy points: "health", "daily routine" and "environment" come up again and again in telc B1 listening and speaking. If you can talk for one minute about your day and one minute about protecting the environment, you are ready for a big part of the oral exam.
Words 4

Vocabulary 4 — work, school & bureaucracy

HIGHEST ROI

telc loves these topics: letters to the boss, calls to the Amt, talking about your job. Learn these words twice as hard.

Almost every telc B1 writing task touches one of these themes: a letter about a course, a complaint to an office, an e-mail to a colleague. If you know this section well, you walk into the exam with a big head start.
How to read the tables: the plural comes after the comma (die Stelle, -n → die Stellen). For verbs you see the Perfekt (the past form you use in speaking): hat = with "haben", ist = with "sein".

🏋️ Fall-Training — watch the article change

Quick reminder: N Nominativ = the doer/subject of the sentence, A Akkusativ = the thing the action happens to, D Dativ = after words like mit/bei/zu or the receiver. Watch the three starred words der Vertrag, die Stelle and das Gehalt change their little word.

Der Vertrag ist fertig.The contract is ready.The contract is the doer/subject of the sentence, so it keeps its dictionary article: der.
Ich unterschreibe den Vertrag.I sign the contract.The contract is the thing being signed, so it is in Akkusativ. Only der changes to den here — die and das words would look exactly the same!
Im Vertrag steht mein Gehalt.My salary is written in the contract.in tells you WHERE something sits, and here that forces Dativ: der becomes dem. Then in + dem melts into one word: im.
Die Stelle ist noch frei.The position is still open.The position is the subject — the sentence is about it — so it keeps its normal article: die.
Ich habe die Stelle bekommen.I got the position.The position is the thing being received — Akkusativ. But die stays die — relax! Only der-words change in Akkusativ.
Er erzählt mir von der Stelle.He tells me about the position.von always forces Dativ. For a die-word that means: die becomes der. Yes, it now LOOKS like a der-word — that is normal, don't panic.
Das Gehalt ist wirklich gut.The salary is really good.The salary is the subject, so nothing happens: das stays das.
Die Firma zahlt das Gehalt pünktlich.The company pays the salary on time.The salary is the thing being paid — Akkusativ. But das stays das — das-words NEVER change in Akkusativ!
Ich bin mit dem Gehalt zufrieden.I am happy with the salary.mit always forces Dativ, so das becomes dem. Nothing else changes.

studieren is only for university. "I'm studying for the exam" = Ich lerne für die Prüfung. Saying "Ich studiere für die Prüfung" is a classic mistake.

🏋️ Fall-Training — watch the article change

Quick reminder: N Nominativ = the doer/subject, A Akkusativ = the thing the action happens to, D Dativ = after words like mit/bei/zu/nach or vor (time) or the receiver. This round: der Kurs, die Prüfung, das Wörterbuch.

Der Kurs beginnt im September.The course starts in September.The course is the doer/subject — it is doing the "starting" — so it keeps its dictionary article: der.
Ich besuche den Kurs zweimal pro Woche.I attend the course twice a week.The course is the thing being attended — Akkusativ. der → den, the classic change. Only der-words do this.
Nach dem Kurs gehe ich nach Hause.After the course I go home.nach (after) always forces Dativ, so der becomes dem.
Die Prüfung dauert zwei Stunden.The exam lasts two hours.The exam is the subject of the sentence, so it keeps its normal article: die.
Ich habe die Prüfung bestanden.I passed the exam.The exam is the thing being passed — Akkusativ. But die stays die — relax! For die-words, Nominativ and Akkusativ look identical.
Vor der Prüfung bin ich nervös.Before the exam I am nervous.vor in time expressions (before the exam) always takes Dativ, so the die-word becomes der.
Das Wörterbuch ist sehr dick.The dictionary is very thick.The dictionary is the subject, so nothing happens: das stays das.
Ich kaufe das Wörterbuch morgen.I am buying the dictionary tomorrow.The dictionary is the thing being bought — Akkusativ. das stays das — das-words never change in Akkusativ, nothing to memorise!
Ich arbeite oft mit dem Wörterbuch.I often work with the dictionary.mit always forces Dativ, so das becomes dem. Nothing else changes.

🏋️ Fall-Training — watch the article change

Quick reminder: N Nominativ = the doer/subject, A Akkusativ = the thing the action happens to, D Dativ = after words like mit/bei/zu/auf (place) or the receiver. This round: der Antrag, die Bank, das Formular.

Der Antrag ist schon fertig.The application is already done.The application is the doer/subject of the sentence, so it keeps its dictionary article: der.
Ich stelle den Antrag heute.I am submitting the application today.The application is the thing being submitted — Akkusativ. Only der changes to den — die and das words would stay the same!
Sie hilft mir beim Antrag.She helps me with the application.bei always forces Dativ: der becomes dem. Then bei + dem melts into one word: beim.
Die Bank öffnet um neun Uhr.The bank opens at nine o'clock.The bank is the subject — it is doing the "opening" — so it keeps its normal article: die.
Ich suche die Bank.I am looking for the bank.The bank is the thing being looked for — Akkusativ. But die stays die — relax! die-words never change in Akkusativ.
Ich gehe morgen zur Bank.I am going to the bank tomorrow.zu always forces Dativ: die becomes der. Then zu + der melts into one word: zur.
Das Formular ist ziemlich lang.The form is quite long.The form is the subject, so nothing happens: das stays das.
Ich fülle das Formular aus.I am filling in the form.The form is the thing being filled in — Akkusativ. das stays das — das-words never change in Akkusativ, zero work for you!
Auf dem Formular fehlt die Unterschrift.The signature is missing on the form.auf tells you WHERE (on the form) — that forces Dativ: das becomes dem.
Memory trickNouns ending in -ung are ALWAYS die — and most come from a verb. Learn the pairs together: sich bewerben → die Bewerbung, anmelden → die Anmeldung, überweisen → die Überweisung, kündigen → die Kündigung, bescheinigen → die Bescheinigung. One rule, dozens of free words.
Memory trickScary "Amt German" is usually a small word you know plus be- or ver-: be + Antrag = beantragen (apply), ver + lang = verlängern (make longer), unter + schreiben = unterschreiben (write your name UNDER the text). And remember: verbs with be-, ver-, über- get no ge- in the Perfekt: hat beantragt, hat verlängert, hat überwiesen.
AUF DEM AMT / AM TELEFON — READY SENTENCES
  • Ich möchte einen Termin vereinbaren. — I would like to arrange an appointment.
  • Ich rufe wegen meiner Anmeldung an. — I am calling about my registration.
  • Welche Unterlagen brauche ich? — Which documents do I need?
  • Ich möchte einen Antrag auf eine Aufenthaltserlaubnis stellen. — I would like to apply for a residence permit.
  • Könnten Sie das bitte wiederholen? — Could you please repeat that?
  • Könnten Sie bitte langsamer sprechen? — Could you please speak more slowly?
  • Bis wann muss ich das Formular abgeben? — By when do I have to hand in the form?
  • Wie lange dauert die Bearbeitung? — How long does the processing take?
  • Ich muss meinen Termin leider verschieben. — Unfortunately I have to postpone my appointment.
  • Können Sie mich bitte mit Frau Müller verbinden? — Can you please connect me with Ms Müller?
  • Vielen Dank für Ihre Hilfe. Auf Wiederhören! — Thank you very much for your help. Goodbye (on the phone)!
Say these ready sentences out loud every day for a week. In the telc speaking exam and in real life at the Amt, these exact sentences do most of the work for you.
Words 5

Vocabulary 5 — travel, transport & city

EXAM FAVOURITE

Trains, hotels, directions — telc loves these topics in Hören, Lesen AND the letter. Learn them well.

How to read the tables: -n / -e / -s after a noun shows the plural ending (die Reise, -n → die Reisen). If the plural changes a vowel, we write the full plural word (der Zug, Züge). Verbs get their Perfekt form: hat = with "haben", ist = with "sein".
